chapter: The Dew Drop, Blue Eagle and visiting stars
title: Nose, the saxophonist Rufus Gore
summary: How the sax player nicknamed Nose settled in New Orleans, was a nice man, and later repaired saxophones.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Is that why they called you Nose?
No. Yeah, it was. Well, other things I can't talk about on.

Yeah. No, no, not necessarily no problems. I mean, he was doing drugs? Uh-uh. Okay. That's why I always thought it was Nose, because he did drugs. No, uh-uh, no. The cocaine? No, he had a big nose, but it was other things.

Yeah, we can't get into that. I just assumed it was drug problems. No, it wasn't drug problems. No, it wasn't drug problems. He was a nice gentleman. He would drink a little bit, but there was no drugs. And he could play, boy. He could play.
Yeah, I heard some of his records on King, and I assumed he was from New Orleans and then recorded, but he came down here.

He came down here and stayed. He stayed, okay. And boy, he could play. And you know what? He got to play, well, he just put his horn up and he was repairing saxophones at Wehrlein. That's where he was when he died. He just put it up and every so often I'd run into him, and he'd talk a lot of crazy talk, you know. But he's a nice fella, but he had his own way of life. That's what I say. He had his own way of life. So.
